summary: This note is a collection of encyclopedic passages about Egypt, covering its history from predynastic times through Ptolemaic rule, Arab conquest and Sufi and Coptic religious history, and modern politics including the 2014 constitution and presidential election. It also covers the Suez Canal, population distribution along the Nile, universities and research institutes, religious recognition and terrorism in the 1980s-2000s, and Red Sea and Mediterranean tourism.
one_line: Wikipedia-derived overview of Egypt's ancient and Islamic history, 2014 politics, religion, population, the Suez Canal, universities and tourism.
key_facts: The Byzantines regained control of Egypt after a brief Sasanian Persian invasion early in the 7th century, during the Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602-628.
Egypt was invaded and conquered by the Muslim Arabs of the Islamic Empire in 639-42.
Cleopatra VII, the last ruler from the Ptolemaic line, committed suicide after the burial of her lover Mark Antony, after Octavian had captured Alexandria.
Egypt recognises only three religions: Islam, Christianity, and Judaism.
On 18 January 2014, the interim government successfully institutionalised a more secular constitution.
Under the constitution, political parties may not be based on 'religion, race, gender or geography'.
The Egyptian presidential election of 26-28 May 2014 had a turnout of 25,578,233 or 47.5%.
Abdel Fattah el-Sisi won the 2014 presidential election with 23.78 million votes, or 96.91%, compared to 757,511 (3.09%) for Hamdeen Sabahi.
In 1973, Egypt and Syria launched the October War, a surprise attack to regain part of the Sinai territory Israel had captured 6 years earlier.
The Suez Canal was opened in November 1869 after 10 years of construction work and connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
With over 90 million inhabitants, Egypt is the most populous country in North Africa and the Arab World.
The great majority of Egypt's people live near the banks of the Nile River, an area of about 40,000 square kilometres (15,000 sq mi).
In the 1990s the Islamist group Al-Gama'a al-Islamiyya engaged in an extended campaign of violence that targeted tourists, foreigners and writers.
The earliest known evidence of Egyptian hieroglyphic inscriptions appeared on Naqada III pottery vessels, dated to about 3200 BC.
Cairo University is ranked 401-500 by the Academic Ranking of World Universities (Shanghai Ranking) and 551-600 by QS World University Rankings.
